title: Spot-Price Oracle Manipulation
summary: A lending desk values collateral using a constant-product AMM's SPOT price. An attacker swaps to pump the price, then borrows far more than the collateral is really worth — draining the desk.
web2Analog: Trusting an attacker-controllable data source as ground truth — like using a client-supplied value for a security decision instead of a trusted server-side source.

identify.question: Why can the lending desk be drained?
options: borrow() transfers tokenB to the caller
It values collateral with amm.priceAinB(), a spot price that one swap can move
identify.explanation: priceAinB() = reserveB / reserveA is the instantaneous (spot) price. A single large swap moves the reserves, so an attacker can inflate the price of their collateral and borrow against the fake valuation.

hints: How does LendingDesk decide how much tokenB your collateral is worth?
priceAinB() = reserveB / reserveA. What happens to that ratio right after a big swap?
Swap to pump A's price, then borrow against a small amount of A at the inflated valuation.

fix.recommendedFix: Never price assets off a manipulable spot price. Use a manipulation-resistant oracle: a time-weighted average price (TWAP) over many blocks, or an external oracle (e.g. Chainlink) with freshness and deviation checks. Spot reserves can be moved within a single transaction (often with a flash loan), so any single-block price is untrustworthy for valuation.
